plan.question: Why is Purnia's completion and employment rate lower than Nalanda's in 2023, and what intervention should be done?
plan.clarification: This file does not contain any information about causes or interventions. It only records how many women enrolled, completed training, and were employed six months later. No variables such as trainer availability, funding, infrastructure, or programme design are present, so a cause cannot be identified from this data alone.

insights.message: This file contains only outcome counts (enrolled, completed, employed) by district and year. It has no columns describing programme inputs, interventions, funding, staffing, or contextual factors that could explain why one district outperforms another. No causal explanation or intervention recommendation can be drawn from this file without guessing. To investigate the cause, additional data such as trainer-to-participant ratios, training duration, local labour market conditions, or programme design differences between districts would be needed.

view.title: Purnia vs Nalanda: Training Completion and Employment (2023)
view.note: Each bar shows the percentage of enrolled women who completed training or were employed six months later in 2023. The gaps in percentage points are stated above. Training completion rate = completed training ÷ women enrolled. Employment rate at 6 months = employed at 6 months ÷ women enrolled. This file cannot explain why the gap exists or recommend an intervention because it contains no information about programme inputs or local conditions.

interpretation_guard.caveat: This data is a synthetic fixture and does not represent real programme outcomes. The file contains no causal variables, so no cause or intervention can be identified from it.
